original_value: In recent years, with the development of compressed sensing theory, sparse representation methods have been concerned by many researchers. Sparse representation can approximate the original image information with less space storage. Sparse representation has been investigated for hyperspectral imagery (HSI) detection, where approximation of testing pixel can be obtained by solving l1-norm minimization. However, l1-norm minimization does not always yield a sufficiently sparse solution when a dictionary is not large enough or atoms present a certain level of coherence. Comparatively, non-convex minimization problems, such as the lp penalties, need much weaker incoherence constraint conditions and may achieve more accurate approximation. Hence, we propose a novel detection algorithm utilizing sparse representation with lp-norm and propose adaptive iterated shrinkage thresholding method (AISTM) for lp-norm non-convex sparse coding. Target detection is implemented by representation of the all pixels employing homogeneous target dictionary (HTD), and the output is generated according to the representation residual. Experimental results for four real hyperspectral datasets show that the detection performance of the proposed method is improved by about 10% to 30% than methods mentioned in the paper, such as matched filter (MF), sparse and low-rank matrix decomposition (SLMD), adaptive cosine estimation (ACE), constrained energy minimization (CEM), one-class support vector machine (OC-SVM), the original sparse representation detector with l1-norm, and combined sparse and collaborative representation (CSCR).

result.paraphrase: With the rise of compressed sensing theory in recent years, sparse representation methods have attracted considerable attention from many researchers. By using less storage space, sparse representation can approximate the information in the original image. It has been studied for hyperspectral imagery (HSI) detection, where a testing pixel can be approximated by solving l1-norm minimization. However, when the dictionary is not large enough or the atoms exhibit a certain degree of coherence, l1-norm minimization does not always produce a sufficiently sparse solution. In comparison, non-convex minimization problems such as lp penalties require much weaker incoherence constraints and can yield more accurate approximations. Therefore, we propose a new detection algorithm based on sparse representation with lp-norm, along with an adaptive iterated shrinkage thresholding method (AISTM) for lp-norm non-convex sparse coding. Target detection is performed by representing all pixels with a homogeneous target dictionary (HTD), and the output is produced according to the representation residual. Experimental results on four real hyperspectral datasets show that the proposed method improves detection performance by about 10% to 30% over the methods mentioned in the paper, including matched filter (MF), sparse and low-rank matrix decomposition (SLMD), adaptive cosine estimation (ACE), constrained energy minimization (CEM), one-class support vector machine (OC-SVM), the original sparse representation detector with l1-norm, and combined sparse and collaborative representation (CSCR).
